thread:
Kevin: heads up — noticed a pattern where our pre-drain lifecycle hook on spot-gpu nodes rarely finishes before the termination notice expires. CA then allocates on-demand and we get a lot of pod migrations + GPU startup churn. anyone seen this?
Maya: saw the same yesterday in eu-west. logs show the hook is stuck copying ~20GB model shards to S3, the IMDS/termination window is only ~2m so it times out.
Devon: yeah copying during preStop is brittle. preStop runs synchronously with kubelet drain flow; if it blocks, node stays uncordoned or CA thinks it's still needed and we get awkward timings.
Amelia: is the hook running in a DaemonSet or as a preStop script in the GPU tenant pods?
Maya: it's a node DaemonSet that runs on termination signal and does an ordered copy of /var/models -> s3://redwood-backups/$NODE. long-running.
Devon: two quick patterns that help: 1) make the preStop quick and spawn a background worker to finish async, 2) on termination signal taint node with "spot-interrupt:NoExecute" immediately so kubelet starts eviction path, then let the background worker finish uploads.
Kevin: example taint command we used in our PoC: ```sh
NODE=$(hostname)
kubectl taint node $NODE spot-interrupt=true:NoExecute --overwrite
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60
```
Maya: adding to that — don't taint before cordon/drain if you have critical system pods without PDBs; they may get evicted instantly. sequence matters: annotate/cordon -> taint -> graceful drain of evictable pods.
Devon: also tweak CA and cluster settings to reduce thrash: increase scaleDownUnneededTime + maxNodeProvisionTime so CA doesn't launch on-demand immediately when a spot starts termination. e.g. CA flags: ```--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --max-node-provision-time=20m --balance-similar-node-groups```
ops-oncall: ops note: for AWS the spot termination notice is ~2 minutes, for GCP preemptible it's immediate in some cases — make the hook tolerant of different provider windows.
sre-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-termination (posted) :eyes:
Amelia: cost angle — keeping a small reserved baseline (5–15% of GPU capacity) as dedicated reduces emergency on-demand bursts. The marginal cost of reserved is lower than repeated on-demand spin-ups during sustained spot churn.
Kevin: action items: 
- Maya/Devon: PR to change preStop -> fire-and-forget pattern + add taint/cordon sequence (canary to 2 nodes).
- Ops: adjust CA flags for 1-week canary in eu-west (scaleDownUnneededTime -> 15m).
- Amelia: model cost delta for 10% reserved vs current fallback rate.
I'll open a short RFC + PR by EOD.
Maya: I'll also add better metrics: count of terminated spot nodes where preStop completed vs timed out, and time-to-healthy for affected pods.
Devon: put a short snippet in the hook that posts status to k8s events + our /infra/state endpoint so CA autoscaler dashboards can correlate. small snippet: ```sh
# on termination
curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/termination-time || true
# quick taint then spawn upload
kubectl taint node $NODE spot-interrupt=true:NoExecute --overwrite &
nohup /usr/local/bin/async-upload.sh /var/models s3://redwood-backups/$NODE &>/var/log/async-upload.log &
exit 0
```
ops-oncall: great — when you open the RFC ping @ops-oncall and I'll reserve a tiny dedicated pool for the canary. :thumbsup:
